cases.description: onboard verb commits to the full chain
verify verb goes straight to launch-and-verify

failed_assertions.value:
The response goes straight to verification of the freshly
generated definition: launch, the verification triplet, and the
action proof loop — not a new analysis or proposal pass. With
no prior context in this single-turn setting, explicitly
routing to launch-and-verify and asking for the missing context
the proof loop needs (project path, workshop name, current
workshop status, which actions were generated) before launching
is acceptable; re-analyzing, re-proposing, or re-opening the
intake menu is not.
failed_assertions.reason: The response does not route to launch-and-verify at all. Instead of asking for the specific context the proof loop needs (project path, workshop name, current status, which actions were generated), it presents a binary A/B menu where option B explicitly offers to re-run `onboard` (re-analysis/re-proposing). This is exactly the behavior the rubric prohibits: re-opening the intake menu and offering to start over rather than proceeding to the verification triplet and action proof loop.
